description: Get the graph edges into or out of one item: a law, an article, a ruling, an opinion, a research study or a Gazette issue. Use this to walk citations and amendments directly, instead of only what get_law and get_article attach automatically. For a law key ("law/<id>") the default scope "all" includes the edges of its articles too (each link keeps its real to_key, e.g. "law/244611/art/37"); scope "law" is the law itself only. Newest first by the date of the text each edge comes from; page with offset and next_offset, total is the number of edges. Not legal advice.

direction.description: "to" (edges that name this item as their target) or "from" (edges this item itself carries)

limit.description: at most this many edges. quote is cut to 600 characters when longer (quote_truncated: true); get_article has the full wording

offset.description: how many edges to skip (next_offset of the previous page)

order.description: by the date of the text the edge comes from (Gazette date, else issue date)

relation.description: narrow to one relation (e.g. "cites", "amend", "repeal"); omit for all

scope.description: for a law key only: "all" (default) adds the edges to or from its articles, "law" is the law itself only

name: get_links
